::: {#sol-four-networks}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
settings = {
    "no normalization or residual connections": {},
    "batch normalization": {"norm": "batch"},
    "residual connections": {"residual": True},
    "batch normalization and residual connections": {"norm": "batch", "residual": True},
}
four_rows = []
for name, options in settings.items():
    loss, acc = train(make_deep(**options))
    four_rows.append({"network": name, "train_loss": loss, "test_accuracy": acc})
four_table = pd.DataFrame(four_rows)
best_network = four_table.loc[four_table["train_loss"].idxmin()]
print(four_table.round(3))
```

The network with `r py$best_network[["network"]]` reaches the lowest training loss,
`r sprintf("%.3f", py$best_network[["train_loss"]])`,
and classifies `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$best_network[["test_accuracy"]])`% of the test images correctly.
The residual network without [batch normalization](#def-batch-norm) reaches `r sprintf("%.3f", py$four_table$train_loss[3])`.
Deep residual networks for images combine the two,
with batch normalization inside each block [@he2016resnet].

:::
